cues.en: Hello, hello again. So moving forward, I'll be assuming that you have a visual understanding of linear transformations and how they're represented with matrices, the way that I've been talking about in the last few videos. If you think about a couple of these linear transformations, you might notice how some of them seem to stretch space out while others squish it on in. One thing that turns out to be pretty useful for understanding one of these transformations is to measure exactly how much it stretches or squishes things. More specifically,
cues.zh: 大家好，又见面了。接下来的内容里，我默认大家已经对线性变换以及如何用矩阵表示它们有了直观的几何理解，就像我在前几个视频中讲的那样。如果你回想几个这样的线性变换，可能会注意到有些变换似乎拉伸了空间，而另一些则挤压了空间。要理解这类变换，事实证明，精确测量出它们拉伸或挤压的程度会非常有帮助。更具体地说，

cues.en: to measure the factor by which the area of a given region increases or decreases. For example, look at the matrix with columns 3, 0, and 0, 2. It scales i hat by a factor of 3 and scales j hat by a factor of 2. Now, if we focus our attention on the 1 by 1 square whose bottom sits on i hat and whose left side sits on j hat, after the transformation, this turns into a 2 by 3 rectangle.
cues.zh: 就是测量出某个特定区域面积放大或缩小的比例。例如，来看一个列向量为 3, 0 和 0, 2 的矩阵。它把 i-hat 放大了 3 倍，把 j-hat 放大了 2 倍。现在，如果我们把注意力集中在一个 1x1 的正方形上，它的底边落在 i-hat 上，左侧边落在 j-hat 上，变换之后，它就变成了一个 2x3 的长方形。

cues.en: Since this region started out with area 1 and ended up with area 6, we can say the linear transformation has scaled its area by a factor of 6. Compare that to a shear whose matrix has columns 1 0 and 1 1, meaning i hat stays in place and j hat moves over to 1 1. That same unit square determined by i hat and j hat gets slanted and turned into a parallelogram.
cues.zh: 因为这个区域一开始面积是 1，最后面积变成了 6，所以可以说这个线性变换把它的面积缩放为原来的 6 倍。把它和一个剪切变换对比：后者的矩阵列向量是 (1,0) 和 (1,1)，也就是 i 帽保持不动，j 帽移到 (1,1)。由 i 帽和 j 帽确定的同一个单位正方形会被斜切，变成一个平行四边形。

cues.en: But the area of that parallelogram is still 1, since its base and height each continue to have length 1. So even though this transformation smushes things about, it seems to leave areas unchanged, at least in the case of that one unit square. Actually though, if you know how much the area of that one single unit square changes, it can tell you how the area of any possible region in space changes.
cues.zh: 但这个平行四边形的面积仍然是 1，因为它的底和高长度都还是 1。所以，尽管这个变换会把东西挤来扭去，它似乎并不改变面积，至少对这个单位正方形如此。不过实际上，只要知道这一个单位正方形的面积变化了多少，就能知道空间中任意可能区域的面积会怎样变化。

cues.en: For starters, notice that whatever happens to one square in the grid has to happen to any other square in the grid, no matter the size. This follows from the fact that grid lines remain parallel and evenly spaced. Then, any shape that's not a grid square can be approximated by grid squares pretty well, with arbitrarily good approximations if you use small enough grid squares.
cues.zh: 首先请注意，网格中任意一个方格的变化，必然会发生在网格中的其他任何方格上，无论大小。这是由网格线始终保持平行且等距这一特性决定的。接着，任何非方格的形状都可以用方格很好地近似，只要方格足够小，就能达到任意精度的近似。

cues.en: So, since the areas of all those tiny grid squares are being scaled by some single amount, the area of the blob as a whole will also be scaled by that same single amount. This very special scaling factor, the factor by which a linear transformation changes any area, is called the determinant of that transformation. I'll show how to compute the determinant of a transformation using its matrix later on in this video, but understanding what it represents is, trust me, much more important than the computation.
cues.zh: 因此，既然所有这些微小方格的面积都按同一比例缩放，那么整个形状的面积也会按完全相同的比例缩放。这个非常特殊的缩放因子，也就是线性变换改变任意面积的比例，就被称为该变换的行列式（determinant）。在本视频的后面，我将演示如何利用变换矩阵来计算行列式，但请相信我，理解它所代表的几何意义，远比计算本身重要得多。

cues.en: For example, the determinant of a transformation would be 3 if that transformation increases the area of a region by a factor of 3. The determinant of a transformation would be ½ if it squishes down all areas by a factor of ½. And the determinant of a 2D transformation is 0 if it squishes all of space onto a line, or even onto a single point. Since then, the area of any region would become 0. That last example will prove to be pretty important.
cues.zh: 比如，如果一个变换把一个区域的面积放大 3 倍，那么这个变换的行列式就是 3。如果一个变换把所有面积都缩小为原来的 ½，那么它的行列式就是 ½。而一个二维变换如果把整个空间压到一条直线上，甚至压到一个点上，它的行列式就是 0。因为这时任何区域的面积都会变成 0。最后一个例子会证明相当重要。

cues.en: It means that checking if the determinant of a given matrix is zero will give a way of computing whether or not the transformation associated with that matrix squishes everything into a smaller dimension. You'll see in the next few videos why this is even a useful thing to think about, but for now I just want to lay down all of the visual intuition, which in and of itself is a beautiful thing to think about. Okay, I need to confess that what I've said so far is not quite right. The full concept of the determinant allows for negative values.
cues.zh: 这意味着，检查一个给定矩阵的行列式是否为零，就能判断与这个矩阵对应的变换是否会把所有东西压到更低的维度。接下来几个视频你会看到，为什么这件事值得思考其实很有用；但现在我只想先把所有直观理解铺开，而这件事本身就值得好好思考。好吧，我得承认，我目前讲的并不完全正确。行列式的完整概念允许负值。

cues.en: But what would the idea of scaling an area by a negative amount even mean? This has to do with the idea of orientation. For example, notice how this transformation gives the sensation of flipping space over. If you were thinking of 2D space as a sheet of paper, a transformation like that one seems to turn over that sheet onto the other side. Any transformations that do this are said to invert the orientation of space. Another way to think about it is in terms of i-hat and j-hat.
cues.zh: 但把面积缩放一个负数究竟是什么意思呢？这与“定向”的概念有关。比如，注意看这个变换是如何给人一种把空间翻转过来的感觉的。如果你把二维空间想象成一张纸，像这样的变换就好像把纸翻到了背面。任何产生这种效果的变换，都被称为反转了空间的定向。另一种理解方式是借助 i-hat 和 j-hat。

cues.en: Notice that in their starting positions, j-hat is to the left of i-hat. If, after a transformation, j-hat is now on the right of i-hat, the orientation of space has been inverted. Whenever this happens, whenever the orientation of space is inverted, the determinant will be negative. The absolute value of the determinant, though, still tells you the factor by which areas have been scaled. For example, the matrix with columns 1, 1 and 2, negative 1 encodes a transformation that has determinant, I'll just tell you,
cues.zh: 注意看它们的初始位置，j-hat 在 i-hat 的左侧。如果在变换之后，j-hat 跑到了 i-hat 的右侧，那么空间的定向就被反转了。只要发生这种情况，只要空间的定向被反转，行列式就会是负的。不过，行列式的绝对值依然表示面积缩放的倍数。举个例子，列向量为 1, 1 和 2, -1 的矩阵所代表的变换，它的行列式——我直接告诉你吧——

cues.en: negative 3. And what this means is that space gets flipped over and areas are scaled by a factor of 3. So why would this idea of a negative area scaling factor be a natural way to describe orientation flipping? Think about the series of transformations you get by slowly letting i-hat get closer and closer to j-hat. As i-hat gets closer, all of the areas in space are getting squished more and more, meaning the determinant approaches zero.
cues.zh: 是 -3。这意味着空间被翻转了，且面积被缩放为原来的 3 倍。那么，为什么用负的面积缩放因子来描述定向翻转会很自然呢？想象一下，让 i-hat 慢慢靠近 j-hat 所得到的一系列变换。随着 i-hat 越来越近，空间中的所有面积都被压得越来越扁，这意味着行列式逐渐趋近于零。

cues.en: Once i-hat lines up perfectly with j-hat, the determinant is zero. Then, if i-hat continues the way that it was going, doesn't it kind of feel natural for the determinant to keep decreasing into the negative numbers? So that's the understanding of determinants in two dimensions. What do you think it should mean for three dimensions? It also tells you how much a transformation scales things, but this time it tells you how much volumes get scaled.
cues.zh: 一旦 i-hat 与 j-hat 完全对齐，行列式就是零。然后，如果 i-hat 继续沿原来的方向走，行列式继续减小、进入负数，是不是也挺自然的？这就是二维中行列式的理解。那你觉得在三维里它应该表示什么？它同样告诉你变换对东西的缩放程度，只不过这次告诉你的是体积被缩放的倍数。

cues.en: Just as in two dimensions, where this is easiest to think about by focusing on one particular square with an area 1 and watching only what happens to it, in three dimensions, it helps to focus your attention on the specific one by one by one cube whose edges are resting on the basis vectors i-hat, j-hat, and k-hat. After the transformation, that cube might get warped into some kind of slanty slanty cube. This shape, by the way, has the best name ever, parallelepiped.
cues.zh: 就像在二维里，最容易理解的方法是盯住一个面积为 1 的特定正方形，只看它发生了什么；在三维里，把注意力集中到那个边落在基向量 i-hat、j-hat、k-hat 上的 1×1×1 立方体会很有帮助。变换之后，这个立方体可能会被扭曲成某种歪歪斜斜的立方体。顺便说，这个形状有个最棒的名字：平行六面体。

cues.en: a name that's made even more delightful when your professor has a nice thick Russian accent. Since this cube starts out with a volume of one, and the determinant gives the factor by which any volume is scaled, you can think of the determinant simply as being the volume of that parallelepiped that the cube turns into. A determinant of zero would mean that all of space is squished onto something with zero volume, meaning either a flat plane, a line, or, in the most extreme case, until a single point.
cues.zh: 这个名称如果由带有浓重俄罗斯口音的教授念出来，会显得更有意思。由于这个立方体最初的体积是 1，而行列式给出的是体积缩放的倍数，所以你可以把行列式简单看作立方体变成平行六面体后的体积。行列式为零意味着整个空间被压缩到了体积为零的物体上，也就是被压缩成一个平面、一条线，在最极端的情况下，甚至是一个单点。

cues.en: Those of you who watch chapter 2 will recognize this as meaning that the columns of the matrix are linearly dependent. Can you see why? What about negative determinants? What should that mean for three dimensions? One way to describe orientation in 3D is with the right hand rule. Point the forefinger of your right hand in the direction of i-hat, stick out your middle finger in the direction of j-hat, and notice how when you point your thumb up, it's in the direction of k-hat. If you can still do that after the transformation,
cues.zh: 看过第二章的观众会明白，这代表矩阵的列向量是线性相关的。你能看出是为什么吗？那负行列式又代表什么呢？这在三维空间中意味着什么？描述三维空间定向的一种方法是用右手定则。将右手的食指指向 i-hat 的方向，中指指向 j-hat 的方向，注意此时当大拇指朝上时，它正对着 k-hat 的方向。如果变换之后你依然能这么做，

cues.en: orientation has not changed and the determinant is positive. Otherwise, if after the transformation it only makes sense to do that with your left hand, orientation has been flipped and the determinant is negative. So if you haven't seen it before, you're probably wondering by now, how do you actually compute the determinant? For a two by two matrix with entries a, b, c, d, the formula is a times d minus b times c. Here's part of an intuition for where this formula comes from.
cues.zh: 定向就没有改变，行列式为正。反之，如果变换后只能用左手才能做到这一点，定向就被翻转了，行列式为负。如果你以前没接触过它，现在可能想知道，究竟该怎么计算行列式？对于元素为 a、b、c、d 的 2x2 矩阵，计算公式是 a 乘以 d 减去 b 乘以 c。下面直观解释一下这个公式从何而来。

cues.en: Let's say that the terms B and C both happened to be zero. Then, the term A tells you how much i-hat is stretched in the x-direction, and the term D tells you how much j-hat is stretched in the y-direction. So, since those other terms are zero, it should make sense that A times D gives the area of the rectangle that our favorite unit square turns into, kind of like the 3-0-0-2 example from earlier. Even if only one of B or C are zero, you'll have a parallelogram with a base A
cues.zh: 假设 B 和 C 这两项碰巧都为零。那么 A 项告诉你 i-hat 在 x 方向上被拉伸了多少，D 项告诉你 j-hat 在 y 方向上被拉伸了多少。所以，既然其他项都是零，A 乘 D 给出我们最爱的单位正方形变成的那个矩形的面积，就说得通了，有点像之前的 3-0-0-2 例子。即使 B 或 C 只有一个为零，你也会得到一个底为 A 的平行四边形

cues.en: and a height d, so the area should still be a times d. Loosely speaking, if both b and c are non-zero, then that b times c term tells you how much this parallelogram is stretched or squished in the diagonal direction. For those of you hungry for a more precise description of this b times c term, here's a helpful diagram if you'd like to pause and ponder. Now, if you feel like computing determinants by hand is something that you need to know,
cues.zh: 高为 d，所以面积仍然应该是 a 乘 d。粗略地说，如果 b 和 c 都非零，那么 b 乘 c 这一项告诉你这个平行四边形在对角线方向上被拉伸或压扁了多少。如果你们想更精确地了解 b 乘 c 这一项，这里有一张有用的图，你可以暂停琢磨一下。现在，如果你觉得手算行列式是你需要掌握的内容，

cues.en: The only way to get it down is to just practice it with a few. There's really not that much I can say or animate that's going to drill in the computation. This is all triply true for three-dimensional determinants. There is a formula, and if you feel like that's something you need to know, you should practice with a few matrices. Or, you know, go watch Sal Khan work through a few. Honestly, though, I don't think that those computations fall within the essence of linear algebra, but I definitely think that understanding what the determinant represents falls within that essence.
cues.zh: 掌握它的唯一办法就是拿几个例子练习。我再怎么说、怎么做动画，也很难把计算过程练熟。这对三维行列式来说更是三倍成立。确实有公式，如果你觉得那是你需要掌握的东西，就应该拿几个矩阵练习。或者，你知道的，去看看 Sal Khan 讲解几道。不过说实话，我不认为这些计算属于线性代数的本质，但我绝对认为，理解行列式代表什么，才属于这个本质。

cues.en: Here's kind of a fun question to think about before the next video. If you multiply two matrices together, the determinant of the resulting matrix is the same as the product of the determinants of the original two matrices. If you tried to justify this with numbers, it would take a really long time, but see if you can explain why this makes sense in just one sentence. Next up, I'll be relating the idea of linear transformations covered so far to one of the areas where linear algebra is most useful, linear systems of equations.
cues.zh: 在看下一个视频之前，有个挺有意思的问题可以思考一下：如果你把两个矩阵相乘，结果矩阵的行列式就等于原本两个矩阵的行列式之积。如果你试图用纯数字去证明这点，会花上非常长的时间，不过你可以试试看，能否只用一句话解释通这背后的道理。接下来，我会将目前为止讲过的线性变换概念，联系到线性代数最实用的领域之一：线性方程组。

cues.en: See you then!
cues.zh: 下期见！
